questions.stem: What does multi-modal data refer to?
options: Data that comes in multiple formats or modalities, such as text, images, audio and video, combined and analysed together
Data stored in more than one relational database table
Structured numbers duplicated across several servers
Data that has been translated into multiple languages
Data collected from more than one country
questions.explanation: Multi-modal data refers to data that comes in multiple formats or modalities. A modality is simply a type or form of data; when different types are combined and analysed together, this is called multi-modal data.

questions.stem: In the context of multi-modal data, what does the word 'modality' mean?
options: A storage location for data
A type or form of data
A statistical average
A governance policy
A machine learning algorithm
questions.explanation: A modality simply means a type or form of data, such as text, images, audio, video or sensor readings.

questions.stem: A social media post is used as an example of multi-modal data. Which combination of modalities does it contain?
options: Only written text and a timestamp
Only images and video
Written text, an image, location information and user reactions
Sensor readings and audio
Transaction history and device fingerprints
questions.explanation: A social media post may include written text, an image, location information and user reactions. Each is a different modality, and analysing them together gives richer insights than any one type alone.

questions.stem: In the customer service example of a multi-modal approach, which steps are combined?
options: Reading an email and replying automatically
Scanning a barcode and updating stock
Storing a photo and tagging it
Analysing a voice recording, converting it to text, examining sentiment and combining it with customer transaction history
Counting calls handled per employee
questions.explanation: The customer service system analyses a voice recording, converts it to text, examines sentiment and combines it with customer transaction history, using more than one type of data to understand the situation.

questions.stem: From a data architecture perspective, what effect does multi-modal data have?
options: It removes the need for metadata management
It allows all data to fit into a single relational table
It simplifies governance controls
It eliminates the need for object storage
It increases complexity because different storage systems may be required and integration needs careful design
questions.explanation: Multi-modal data increases architectural complexity. Text might sit in relational databases, images in object storage and streaming audio in specialised systems, so integrating them requires careful design, metadata management and governance controls.

questions.stem: Why does a fraud detection system that analyses only transaction numbers illustrate the value of multi-modal data?
options: Because it may miss patterns that adding customer behaviour, device fingerprints and communication patterns would reveal
Because transaction numbers cannot be stored in databases
Because fraud detection requires only images
Because a single modality always produces more accurate results
Because transaction numbers are not considered data
questions.explanation: A fraud detection system analysing only transaction numbers may miss patterns. Adding customer behaviour, device fingerprints and communication patterns gives deeper understanding; combining modalities often leads to better accuracy and stronger insights.

questions.stem: In the Grade 7 example of multi-modal data, how does the teacher build a complete picture of a student's learning?
options: By looking only at exam scores
By combining exam scores, class participation, an oral presentation and homework
By asking the student's parents
By comparing the student with the class average only
By reviewing attendance alone
questions.explanation: The teacher does not look only at exam scores; she also observes class participation, listens to an oral presentation and checks homework. Each is a different type of data, and together they give a complete picture, just like multi-modal data.

questions.stem: In the example of recognising a friend, which modalities does a person naturally combine?
options: Temperature, weight and height
Location, time and date
What they say (audio), how they look (image) and how they write messages (text)
Their exam scores and homework
Their transaction history and device fingerprint
questions.explanation: You identify a friend not only by what they say (audio) but also by how they look (image) and perhaps how they write messages (text). The brain naturally combines multiple data types, and modern AI systems try to do the same.

questions.stem: In traditional systems, before multi-modal data became common, what form did most data take?
options: Video streams
Voice recordings
Sensor readings
Structured text or numbers stored in tables
Images in object storage
questions.explanation: In traditional systems, most data was structured text or numbers stored in tables. Today organisations also deal with text, images, audio, video, sensor readings and more.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT named as a modality that multi-modal data may include?
options: Text
Images
Audio
Video
Blockchain ledgers
questions.explanation: Multi-modal data is described as combining forms such as text, images, audio, video, sensor readings and structured records. Blockchain ledgers are not named as a modality.
